transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-12-09 16:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Darren Cole (Elmwood CTO), Priya Rao (Head of ML), Samir Khan (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto): exploring Dedicated capacity for latency-sensitive LLM workloads, isolation and compliance needs, burst/buffer strategy, and next steps to run benchmarks + share security docs.

Topics: Dedicated capacity, reserved GPUs, VPC/private deployment options, burst capacity, autoscaling policies, SOC2/KMS, pricing, benchmarks

00:00 Darren: hey thanks for squeezing us in, we, we wanted to go over what Dedicated looks like for us.
00:07 Maya: yeah for sure — thanks for the time. quick intro, i'm maya, AE, and luis is our SE, he'll take the technical.
00:13 Luis: hey everyone, hi, good to meet you.
00:15 Darren: good to meet you both. so, quick context: elmwood is evaluating moving our transformer-based ranking and customer chat models to a hosted solution but with isolation. we want reserved capacity not burstable hosted. main drivers: latency under 150ms tail for chat, predictable cost, and compliance for PII.
00:33 Maya: gotcha. and you said chat + ranking — can you give ballpark qps and sequence lengths?
00:39 Priya: sure, the chat workload averages 10 qps now, peaks to about 60 in certain windows. seq lengths average 512 tokens for chat, ranking runs shorter prompts but higher concurrency — about 200 qps during overnight batch runs. token mix is like 70% short inference, 30% longer context.
00:56 Luis: ok that's helpful. when you say "reserved", are you thinking dedicated machines that only run elmwood's models?
01:02 Samir: yes, dedicated GPUs, isolated vpc, we need tenant isolation for audit reasons. we also want the ability to burst beyond reserved capacity for busy days but with caps.
01:11 Maya: that's exactly where Redwood Dedicated sits — reserved GPU pools with private networking. for bursts we offer a burst pool or fallback to hosted with policy controls. question for you: how important is data not leaving your VPC vs us offering a private control plane?
01:25 Darren: high. for regulated customers we need full network separation, logs stored in our account, and KMS managed keys. we also have internal auditors that will want SOC2 artifacts.
01:34 Luis: we support Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) with customer-managed KMS and audit logs. for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS and push audit logs to your SIEM; some customers opt for a private control plane too.
01:44 Priya: how does bursting work? will we lose isolation if we burst to shared hosted?
01:49 Luis: good q — bursting can be configured two ways: 1) burst to a customer-dedicated cold pool (reserved but lower priority), or 2) burst to our shared-hosted nodes. the second option leaves some data movement that you might be uncomfortable with. for strict isolation you'd use intra-customer burst pools or expand committed capacity.
02:09 Samir: how about autoscaling? can we set min/max GPUs and rules around tail latency?
02:14 Luis: yes, autoscaling in Dedicated is policy-driven. you can set min/max GPU counts, target latency SLOs, and prefer performance-optimized kernels or quantized variants when scaling. we also do dynamic batching and KV cache reuse to keep costs down.
02:28 Darren: you mentioned KV cache — can you explain how that works with multiple tenants and context reuse?
02:33 Luis: sure. KV cache stores transformer state; for Dedicated it's per-tenant per-model. we keep the cache on the serving nodes so warm sessions reuse slots, which reduces effective latency. note: small transcription glitch — sometimes our docs say "KV cash" in auto text — sorry.
02:47 Priya: and for model versions, can we pin to a specific model and rollout? we need controlled rollouts for quality checks.
02:53 Maya: absolutely — we support model pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to previous versions. Redwood Console gives you per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdowns.
03:03 Samir: compliance-wise — we need SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS with customer HSM. do you integrate with internal KMS/HSM?
03:11 Luis: yes, we integrate with customer KMS providers and can do HSM-backed key management for output encryption at rest. SSO via SAML and fine-grained RBAC are supported. we'll share the security pack.
03:19 Darren: pricing — how does reserved capacity pricing look relative to hosted?
03:23 Maya: reserved is commit-based; you pay a monthly fee for reserved GPU pools plus a smaller per-token or per-instance runtime charge. it ends up lower unit cost at scale compared to hosted, and you get capacity guarantees and SLAs.
03:34 Priya: for our batch ranking at 200 qps overnight, do you recommend separate pools?
03:38 Luis: yes, many customers isolate high-concurrency batch workloads into separate GPU pools or schedule them in off-peak windows. you can also run different model variants (quantized for batch vs high-precision for chat) to optimize cost.
03:50 Samir: curious about burst caps — can we set a hard cap to avoid runaway spend?
03:55 Maya: yes you can set hard caps and alerts; by default bursts are quiesced when budget thresholds are hit.
03:59 Darren: latency SLA — can you commit to p95 or p99? we care about p99 under load.
04:05 Luis: we target p95 and p99 SLAs on Dedicated, depends on model and sequence lengths. we can size the pool to meet p99 95% of the time; for absolute guarantees we typically recommend overprovisioning or reserve higher-tier GPUs.
04:19 Priya: do you support quantized models? we can accept a small quality tradeoff for big cost savings.
04:24 Luis: yes, quantization profiles are part of Redwood Optimize — we can recommend quantization and kernels that match your workload, and we can run A/B quality tests during benchmarking.
04:34 Maya: quick qual question — timeline for procurement? any stakeholders we should loop in?
04:38 Darren: procurement and security will need to be involved. goal is to decide by end of Q1 2027, procurement process will take 4-6 weeks after technical sign-off.
04:48 Maya: great — next steps we'll send pricing, and security docs, and Luis will schedule a benchmark run.
04:53 Luis: i can run a 3-day benchmark using a subset of your prompts to measure latency and throughput and compare dedicated vs hosted. we'll need sample prompts and token profiles.
04:59 Priya: we'll share a scrubbed set of prompts and expected SLAs.
05:02 Samir: also want network diagram and expected traffic flow, we'll need to see where audit logs go.
05:07 Maya: noted. i'll attach the network diagram template and SOC2 pack.
05:10 Darren: any limitations on model types — do you support our in-house finetuned models?
05:14 Luis: yes, you can bring your own model artifacts. we support standard transformer formats and containerized model envs. some optimization may be required for kernel selection and quantization.
05:26 Priya: what about on-prem option — we have one customer segment that disallows cloud.
05:30 Luis: we offer Private on-prem deployments; the control plane can be private and the serving runtime runs in your cluster. that path tends to have longer lead time and a different commercial model.
05:42 Darren: can we see a cost comparison example — say 8 reserved A100s vs hosted?
05:46 Maya: yes we'll include a cost model spreadsheet with throughput assumptions; it will show committed vs pay-as-you-go and include burst pricing.
05:54 Samir: SLA credits and support levels?
05:56 Maya: dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and priority support; enterprise packages include 24/7 on-call and quarterly reviews.
06:02 Priya: any gotchas we should know?
06:05 Luis: eyeballing things: 1) cold start for very long contexts if cache miss; 2) model pinning means you'll need a CI flow for rollouts; 3) bursting to shared nodes if not configured will introduce data-plane movement — so configure the desired burst behavior.
06:21 Darren: perfect — recap then?
06:24 Maya: recap: we'll send pricing + capacity options, security pack (SOC2/ISO + network template), schedule a 3-day benchmark using your scrubbed prompts, and follow up on autoscaling deep dive.
06:35 Darren: sounds good. i'll get procurement and security on the thread.
06:38 Priya: action items: we'll share prompts and token logs, and schedule time with Luis for benchmarks.
06:45 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday with the docs and a proposed benchmark window.
06:50 Luis: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional words mis-typed (K-V cache as KV cash), some speaker turns merged; overall medium-quality auto transcript.

References (shared during call): Redwood security pack (link sent after call), Dedicated pricing spreadsheet (to be shared), benchmark harness template (Luis to share).
